newsitem.title: USA: NY/NJ Port sees $1.2 bln JFK bonds in Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: NY/NJ Port sees $1.2 bln JFK bonds in Q1 1997.

text.p: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey expects to issue about $1.2 billion of bonds for New York City's JFK International Airport in the first quarter of 1997, George Marlin, the agency's executive director, said Tuesday.
Marlin, speaking at an industry conference in Manhattan, said the agency is also "working on a five-year capital plan of about $6.4 billion."
Of the five-year plan's total, he said "well over 60 percent" would be spent on the New York side of the Hudson River, in accordance with an agreement between the governors of the two states.
Over the last several years, spending by the authority has averaged about 52 percent for New York and 48 percent for New Jersey, Marlin said.
The bonds for JFK Airport would be used for a new international arrivals building.
